subject: Post-demo: Medinova private connectivity & integration next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@medinova-health.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood integration + private connectivity — post-demo recap

Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the Medinova POC.

Context from call:
- Primary goal: embed Redwood inference into Medinova’s clinical-ng app for real-time summarization and contextual search (embeddings + reranker) while meeting your network/security constraints.
- Host: Medinova runs in AWS (multi-account), strict egress policy, and uses internal DNS and a private VPC with no public-facing services by default.

Key technical topics we touched on (for follow-up):
1) Connectivity options — PrivateLink vs. allowlist egress
   - We need to confirm whether you prefer an AWS PrivateLink endpoint (Private connectivity) or the simpler static egress IP allowlist (NAT) approach for the POC.
2) Auth & encryption
   - API keys are standard for hosted API access; we also support mutual TLS (mTLS) for customer-side client certs and can integrate with KMS-backed certs on Private deployments.
3) SDK setup & routing
   - We'll provide our Node/Python SDK + an integration checklist. Routing can be configured to pin traffic to a regional cluster for latency (us-west-2) and to fall back to a lower-cost model variant if capacity is constrained.
4) Structured output & tool-calling
   - Structured JSON output and function-calling are supported; we'll share a canonical schema example you can validate against.
5) Embeddings & reranker concerns
   - Embeddings are tenant-isolated; you can enable at-rest encryption and control retention. Reranking can be performed in your environment if you prefer to keep vectors on-prem.

Immediate asks from our side (so we can scope the workshop):
- Confirm preferred connectivity option: PrivateLink (AWS endpoint) or IP allowlist/NAT egress.
- Your VPC CIDR(s) and whether you have a dedicated integration subnet we can target.
- Any specific DNS constraints (do you require internal DNS forwarding / split-horizon?).
- mTLS requirement (yes/no) and cert rotation cadence if yes.

Proposed next step:
- Technical workshop with Rishi (networking) and Priyom (solutions engineering) to scope the Private connectivity setup and SDK auth flow. Can you do Wed 3/11 9am or Thu 3/12 1pm PT?

Attachments: we’ll follow up with a lightweight network diagram and a private-connectivity checklist (will include required ports, sample security group rules, expected egress ranges).

Thanks — I’ll wait for the connectivity preference and preferred workshop slot.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Chen <alex@medinova-health.com>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood integration + private connectivity — post-demo recap

Hi Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our security/network side: 

- We strongly prefer PrivateLink for production if Redwood supports it. For the initial POC we could accept NAT + IP allowlist if PrivateLink lead time is long.
- Our infra: AWS us-west-2 primary, VPC peered across accounts. We have a strict egress whitelist; all outbound traffic must be from a known set of IPs.
- DNS: we operate split-horizon private DNS. If you use PrivateLink we’ll want your service DNS to resolve to the interface endpoint IPs internally (we can handle the route53/private hosted zone).
- mTLS: preferred for production. For POC, short-lived API keys are acceptable but we’ll need an mTLS plan and cert rotation policy for production.

Questions for the workshop prep:
1) If we go PrivateLink, what is Redwood’s ownership of the endpoint (service side)? Any cross-account requirements?
2) If we must do NAT + allowlist for the POC, can you provide the precise egress IPs (or a small CIDR set) to add to our outbound policy?
3) For embeddings: will vectors leave our VPC? We need assurance they’re encrypted and tenant isolated; can Medinova opt to store embeddings solely in our account (on-prem/private deployment) later?

We can do Wed 3/11 9am PT for the workshop. Please send dial-in and any pre-reads.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Director, Infrastructure & Security | Medinova Health
alex@medinova-health.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@medinova-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood integration + private connectivity — technical notes & checklist (attached)

Alex / Marissa — thanks, copying the technical checklist and a first-pass network diagram (attached). Summary answers below and a proposed minimal POC plan.

Short answers to your numbered questions:
1) PrivateLink ownership & cross-account: Redwood exposes a regional service name for AWS PrivateLink. For hosted PrivateLink, Redwood creates the service (our account), you create an interface endpoint in your VPC and accept the service. Cross-account is standard (no peering required). We’ll provide the service name and a one-time accept token if required.

2) Egress IPs for NAT allowlist: for customers doing NAT egress we can provide a small, stable IP range for the regional cluster used by your account for the POC. Sample (reserve): 34.201.72.192/29 and 3.88.130.16/29 — we’ll give final /29 blocks in the checklist attachment and can publish an allowlist JSON for your automation.

3) Embeddings handling: for Redwood hosted API, embeddings and vectors are encrypted at rest with tenant separation. For a strict requirement to keep vectors in your account, we offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) where vector storage runs inside your environment. Hybrid models exist where vectors are computed locally and only ids/metas are used for reranking in our service.

Technical POC plan (minimum viable):
- Step 0: Exchange contact for infra SRE + provide target VPC CIDR and a test subnet.
- Step 1: Create either interface endpoint (PrivateLink) or configure NAT egress path and add temporary allowlist (we’ll provide IP blocks).
- Step 2: Issue temporary POC API key; optionally deploy client mTLS cert (we can support both).
- Step 3: Run a smoke test: 5k short inference calls + embedding write/read test.
- Step 4: Validate latency and routing to the pinned regional cluster; capture token-level logs for the first 24 hours.

Networking hints in the checklist (attached):
- Ports: 443 (TLS) only for API traffic; PrivateLink uses the ENI IPs internally.
- DNS: recommend adding a private hosted zone that routes your service FQDN to the interface endpoint addresses for PrivateLink.
- Security Groups: allow outbound to Redwood egress IPs / internal ENI IPs for PrivateLink; restrict to only the integration subnet.
- mTLS: we accept client certs issued by your CA. We also support mutual auth via our managed CA if you prefer.

Attachments: network_diagram_v1.png (logical layout) & redwood_private_connectivity_checklist.pdf (detailed steps, sample SG rules, allowlist JSON).

I’ll be on the Wed 3/11 09:00 PT call. If you can share the test VPC CIDR and a point-of-contact from your infra team beforehand, we’ll prepare the PrivateLink service name and the temporary allowlist JSON.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
